scope: Manual controlled experiments; no pins, inline asm or compiler trace. Router setup failed on obsolete unused m2c_macros.h include; no permutation output contributed.
observations: Separate stores in the two mode arms preserve distinct global loads (UID60 and UID97) and HIGH pseudos (r91 and r100) through CSE. Late cross-jumping merges the stores after allocation.
Base_1 global r83 work and r84 offset each have refs=4 and span=9. They conflict with one another and v0/v1, with no copy preferences. Work allocates first into a0.
Base_2 changes only local declaration order. Offset becomes r83, work r84; global allocno tie-break now assigns offset=a0, work=a1. Object distance goes 27 to 0.
Ported base_3 also scores exactly with normal headers and typed callee parameter.
limits: No runtime CSE path tracing was performed. The observed preservation precedes allocation, disproving the previous assertion that reload must create the second load.
Declaration ordering is relevant to this demonstrated GLOBAL priority tie; it does not specify local quantity order.
